```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2); library(patchwork)
  library(ggrepel); library(ARTool); library(car); library(MASS)
  library(FSA); library(rcompanion)
})
# MASS masks dplyr::select and dplyr::filter; pin them back.
select <- dplyr::select; filter <- dplyr::filter
set.seed(42)
```

```{r constants}
INK    <- "#0b0b0b"; INK2 <- "#52514e"; MUTED <- "#898781"
GRID_C <- "#e1e0d9"; SURFACE <- "#ffffff"
ACCENT <- "#c1121f"
# The one neutral ramp of the thesis: constant hue and chroma, five rungs.
WARM   <- c("#aaa8a2", "#888680", "#65635d", "#46443f", "#292823")
FONT   <- "URWPalladio"
FIGDIR <- "figures"; dir.create(FIGDIR, showWarnings = FALSE)
FIG_W  <- 5.9; FIG_H <- 3.4

ALPHA     <- 0.05
FACTORS   <- c("roi_size", "max_crops", "mode", "thresh", "pool_ks")
RESPONSES <- c("F1", "MAE")
BLOCK     <- "replica"
RESP_LABELS <- c(F1 = "F1-score", MAE = "MAE")
BLUE <- "#2a78d6"; ORANGE <- "#eb6834"; VIOLET <- "#4a3aa7"; YELLOW <- "#eda100"
RESP_COLORS <- c(F1 = BLUE, MAE = ORANGE)
MODE_COLORS <- c(average = VIOLET, majority_voting = YELLOW)
SLATE <- c("#9aa6b4", "#7d8998", "#626d7c", "#46505d", "#2a313b")
SELECTED <- list(roi_size = 9, max_crops = 90, mode = "average",
                 thresh = 0.58, pool_ks = 9)

theme_thesis <- function(base = 8.5) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base, base_family = FONT) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(colour = INK, family = FONT),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = GRID_C, linewidth = 0.5 / .pt),
      panel.border = element_blank(),
      axis.line  = element_line(colour = MUTED, linewidth = 0.6 / .pt),
      axis.ticks = element_line(colour = INK2,  linewidth = 0.6 / .pt),
      axis.ticks.length = unit(1.5, "pt"),
      axis.text  = element_text(colour = INK2, size = 6.3, family = FONT),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = INK, size = 7.2, family = FONT),
      strip.text = element_text(colour = INK, size = 7.2, family = FONT),
      plot.title = element_blank(), plot.subtitle = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(1, 8, 7, 1),
      legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "horizontal",
      legend.title = element_text(colour = INK, size = 7.2, family = FONT),
      legend.text  = element_text(colour = INK2, size = 6.0, family = FONT),
      legend.key.width = unit(8, "pt"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "pt"),
      legend.margin = margin(t = -1, b = 0), legend.box.spacing = unit(2, "pt"),
      legend.background = element_blank(), legend.key = element_blank(),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = SURFACE, colour = NA))
}
theme_set(theme_thesis())
save_fig <- function(p, name, w = FIG_W, h = FIG_H)
  ggsave(file.path(FIGDIR, paste0(name, ".pdf")), p, width = w, height = h,
         device = "pdf", family = FONT)
```

```{r load}
raw <- read.csv("grid_results.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df <- raw %>%
  rename(F1 = f1_center, MAE = mae,
         precision_point = p_center, recall_point = r_center,
         F1_iou = f1, precision_iou = precision, recall_iou = recall) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(c(FACTORS, BLOCK)), factor))
c(rows = nrow(df), configs = nrow(distinct(df[FACTORS])), replicas = nlevels(df[[BLOCK]]))
```

```{r level-keys}
KEYSEP  <- "\u001f"
LEV_ALL <- unlist(lapply(FACTORS, function(f)
  paste(f, levels(df[[f]]), sep = KEYSEP)))

lev_key <- function(fac, lev) factor(paste(fac, lev, sep = KEYSEP), levels = LEV_ALL)
# The `mode` panel is the narrowest and carries the longest label, so the key is
# stripped and the underscore becomes a line break: "majority_voting" would
# otherwise run into "average".
scale_x_levels <- function()
  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x)
    sub("_", "_\n", sub(paste0(".*", KEYSEP), "", x)))
# On a horizontal layout the labels have the full width of the margin, so they
# need no break.
# `limits = rev` makes the levels read downwards in the same order as the rows
# of the thesis tables; a discrete y axis would otherwise start at the bottom.
scale_y_levels <- function()
  ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = rev,
                            labels = function(x) sub(paste0(".*", KEYSEP), "", x))
```

# Assumption verification

```{r assumptions}
cellres <- df %>% group_by(across(all_of(FACTORS))) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(RESPONSES), ~ .x - mean(.x), .names = "res_{.col}")) %>% ungroup()

# Population skewness and excess kurtosis, reported beside the test: they say
# how the residuals depart from normal, which W alone does not.
skew <- function(x) { m <- mean(x); n <- length(x)
  sum((x - m)^3) / n / (sum((x - m)^2) / n)^1.5 }
exkurt <- function(x) { m <- mean(x); n <- length(x)
  sum((x - m)^4) / n / (sum((x - m)^2) / n)^2 - 3 }
norm_rows <- lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) {
  x <- cellres[[paste0("res_", r)]]
  w <- shapiro.test(x)
  data.frame(response = r, W = unname(w$statistic), p = w$p.value,
             skew = skew(x), exkurt = exkurt(x))
})
normality <- bind_rows(norm_rows)

lev_rows <- list()
for (r in RESPONSES) for (f in FACTORS) {
  lt <- car::leveneTest(df[[r]] ~ df[[f]], center = median)
  lev_rows[[paste(r, f)]] <- data.frame(response = r, factor = f,
                                        F = lt[1, "F value"], p = lt[1, "Pr(>F)"])
}
levene <- bind_rows(lev_rows)
# Persisted so the thesis table is formatted from the same numbers rather than
# recomputed: SciPy's shapiro underflows to p = 0 where R reports 1.4e-46.
knitr::kable(normality, digits = 4, caption = "Shapiro-Wilk on within-cell residuals")
knitr::kable(levene, digits = 4, caption = "Levene (Brown-Forsythe) per factor")
```

```{r fig-normality, fig.width=FIG_W, fig.height=5.0}
resid_long <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r)
  data.frame(response = r, value = cellres[[paste0("res_", r)]])))
# A normal density with the residuals' own standard deviation, to compare shape
# rather than scale.
norm_curve <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) {
  x <- cellres[[paste0("res_", r)]]
  g <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 400)
  data.frame(response = r, value = g, dens = dnorm(g, 0, sd(x)))
}))
p_dist <- ggplot(resid_long, aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 60,
                 fill = MUTED, alpha = 0.40, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(data = norm_curve, aes(value, dens),
            colour = ACCENT, linewidth = 0.7 / .pt, linetype = "32") +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  labs(x = "Within-cell residual", y = "Density")

qq <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) {
  x <- cellres[[paste0("res_", r)]]
  data.frame(response = r, theo = qqnorm(x, plot.it = FALSE)$x,
             samp = qqnorm(x, plot.it = FALSE)$y)
}))
# The reference line goes through the first and third quartiles, as a Q-Q line
# must: the residuals keep their own units, so an identity line would be drawn
# at slope 1 against quantiles that run from -3 to 3 and come out near vertical.
qline <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) {
  x  <- cellres[[paste0("res_", r)]]
  qs <- quantile(x, c(.25, .75)); ts <- qnorm(c(.25, .75))
  sl <- unname(diff(qs) / diff(ts))
  data.frame(response = r, slope = sl, intercept = unname(qs[1]) - sl * ts[1])
}))
p_qq <- ggplot(qq, aes(theo, samp)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.25, colour = MUTED) +
  geom_abline(data = qline, aes(slope = slope, intercept = intercept),
              colour = ACCENT, linewidth = 0.7 / .pt, linetype = "32") +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Within-cell residual")

# One figure rather than two stacked by LaTeX: patchwork aligns the panels, so
# the four plot areas share their left edge.  Two separately saved PDFs cannot,
# because each sizes its own margin from the width of its own axis labels.
p <- p_dist / p_qq
print(p); save_fig(p, "grid_normality_diagnostics", h = 5.0)
```

```{r fig-variance, fig.width=FIG_W, fig.height=2.5}
# Residual against the cell mean that produced it: the fitted value of the
# saturated model.  Equal variances would show a band of constant width.
sl <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) data.frame(
  response = r,
  fitted = cellres[[r]] - cellres[[paste0("res_", r)]],
  resid  = cellres[[paste0("res_", r)]])))
p <- ggplot(sl, aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.25, colour = MUTED) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = ACCENT, linewidth = 0.7 / .pt, linetype = "32") +
  facet_wrap(~response, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  labs(x = "Cell mean (fitted value)", y = "Within-cell residual")
print(p); save_fig(p, "grid_variance_diagnostics", h = 2.5)
```

```{r transformations}
cell_resid <- function(y, d) y - ave(y, interaction(d[FACTORS], drop = TRUE))
bc_fit <- function(y, d) {
  form <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(FACTORS, collapse = " * ")))
  bc <- MASS::boxcox(form, data = cbind(d, y = y), plotit = FALSE,
                     lambda = seq(-3, 3, 0.005))
  keep <- bc$x[bc$y > max(bc$y) - qchisq(.95, 1) / 2]
  list(lambda = bc$x[which.max(bc$y)], lo = min(keep), hi = max(keep))
}
bc <- setNames(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) bc_fit(df[[r]], df)), RESPONSES)
boxcox_tf <- function(y, l) if (abs(l) < 1e-8) log(y) else (y^l - 1) / l
scales_for <- function(r) { l <- bc[[r]]$lambda
  list(identity = function(y) y, sqrt = sqrt, cbrt = function(y) y^(1/3),
       log = log, `1/x` = function(y) 1 / y,
       `box-cox` = function(y) boxcox_tf(y, l)) }

transformations <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) {
  y0 <- df[[r]]
  bind_rows(lapply(names(scales_for(r)), function(nm) {
    z <- scales_for(r)[[nm]](y0); e <- cell_resid(z, df)
    sw <- shapiro.test(e)
    rej <- sum(sapply(FACTORS, function(f)
      leveneTest(z ~ df[[f]], center = median)$`Pr(>F)`[1] < ALPHA))
    sdr <- max(sapply(FACTORS, function(f) {
      m <- tapply(z, df[[f]], sd); max(m) / min(m) }))
    data.frame(response = r, transform = nm,
               lambda = if (nm == "box-cox") bc[[r]]$lambda else NA_real_,
               W = unname(sw$statistic), p_shapiro = sw$p.value,
               levene_rejects = rej, sd_ratio_max = sdr,
               both_hold = sw$p.value > ALPHA && rej == 0)
  }))
}))
transformations
```

# The factorial ART model

```{r art-fit}
fit_art <- function(resp)
  art(as.formula(sprintf("%s ~ %s + Error(%s)", resp,
                         paste(FACTORS, collapse = " * "), BLOCK)), data = df)
fits <- setNames(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) list(model = fit_art(r))), RESPONSES)
```

```{r art-effects, cache=TRUE, cache.lazy=FALSE}
SS_TYPE <- "III"   # ARTool's default; pinned rather than inherited

effect_table <- function(resp, type = SS_TYPE) {
  a  <- as.data.frame(anova(fits[[resp]]$model, type = type))
  Fv <- if ("F value" %in% names(a)) a[["F value"]] else a[["F"]]
  dr <- if ("Df.res"  %in% names(a)) a$Df.res       else a[["Den Df"]]
  tm <- if ("Term"    %in% names(a)) as.character(a$Term) else rownames(a)
  data.frame(response = resp, effect = tm,
             order = lengths(strsplit(tm, ":")), df = a$Df, df_res = dr,
             F = Fv, p = a[["Pr(>F)"]],
             eta_p2 = Fv * a$Df / (Fv * a$Df + dr), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
eff <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, effect_table))
for (r in RESPONSES) {
  k <- sum(eff$response == r)
  if (k != 31) warning(sprintf("%s: %d effects, expected 31", r, k))
}

# Types I, II and III must coincide here; confirm rather than assert.
for (r in RESPONSES) {
  g <- function(ty) effect_table(r, ty)$eta_p2
  cat(sprintf("%s: max |III-II| = %.3g, max |III-I| = %.3g\n",
              r, max(abs(g("III") - g("II"))), max(abs(g("III") - g("I")))))
}
```

```{r art-print}
for (r in RESPONSES) {
  e <- eff[eff$response == r, ]
  cat("\n=====", r, "=====\n")
  print(e[order(e$order, -e$eta_p2), c("effect", "order", "df", "p", "eta_p2")],
        row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
}
```

```{r main-order}
main <- eff %>% filter(order == 1) %>% arrange(response, desc(eta_p2))
knitr::kable(main[, c("response", "effect", "df", "F", "p", "eta_p2")], digits = 4)
ord <- sapply(RESPONSES, function(r) {
  m <- main[main$response == r, ]
  paste(sprintf("%s (%.3f)", m$effect, m$eta_p2), collapse = " > ")
})
```

```{r inter}
big <- eff %>% filter(eta_p2 >= 0.30) %>% arrange(response, desc(eta_p2))
knitr::kable(big[, c("response", "effect", "order", "df", "p", "eta_p2")], digits = 4,

top <- eff[which.max(eff$eta_p2), ]
```

```{r fig-effects, fig.width=FIG_W, fig.height=4.4}
# One panel per response, each ordered by its own magnitude: a single panel
# ordered by the mean of the two shows neither ranking.  The key trick of the
# level-ordering helpers is reused here to order within a facet.
# 0.14 is the threshold the thesis table calls large, so the figure and the
# shading of that table cut at the same place.
rank_df <- eff %>% filter(eta_p2 >= 0.14) %>%
  arrange(response, eta_p2) %>%
  mutate(key = factor(paste(response, effect, sep = KEYSEP),
                      levels = unique(paste(response, effect, sep = KEYSEP))))
p <- ggplot(rank_df, aes(eta_p2, key)) +
  geom_col(fill = MUTED, width = 0.58) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", eta_p2)), hjust = -0.18,
            size = 6.4 / .pt, colour = INK2) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.13))) +
  # space = "free_y" gives each panel a height proportional to its own number
  # of bars: 6 effects are large on F1 against 18 on the MAE.
  facet_grid(response ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y",
             labeller = labeller(response = RESP_LABELS)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(paste0(".*", KEYSEP), "", x)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = GRID_C, linewidth = 0.5 / .pt))
print(p); save_fig(p, "grid_effect_size_ranking", h = 4.4)
```

# Post-hoc contrasts

```{r artcon}
con_rows <- list()
for (r in RESPONSES) for (f in FACTORS) {
  cs <- tryCatch({
    x <- as.data.frame(summary(art.con(fits[[r]]$model, f, adjust = "holm")))
    x$response <- r; x$factor <- f; x
  }, error = function(e) { cat("art.con failed for", r, "/", f, ":", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  if (!is.null(cs)) con_rows[[paste(r, f)]] <- cs
}
if (length(con_rows)) {
  con <- bind_rows(con_rows)
  knitr::kable(head(con, 25), digits = 4)
} else cat("no contrasts obtained; art.con() does not support the error structure used above.\n")
```

# Blocking factor

```{r blocking}
wide <- df %>% mutate(cfg = interaction(!!!rlang::syms(FACTORS), drop = TRUE))
fr <- lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) {
  m <- matrix(wide[[r]][order(wide$cfg, wide$replica)],
              ncol = nlevels(wide$replica), byrow = TRUE)
  ft <- friedman.test(m)
  data.frame(response = r, chi2 = unname(ft$statistic), df = unname(ft$parameter),
             p = ft$p.value, kendall_W = unname(ft$statistic) / (nrow(m) * (ncol(m) - 1)))
})
blocking <- bind_rows(fr)
knitr::kable(blocking, digits = 4)
```

```{r fig-replica, fig.width=5.9, fig.height=2.4}
print(p)

ggsave(path, p, width = 5.9, height = 2.4, device = "pdf", family = FONT)
```

# Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn screening

```{r kruskal}
kw <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) bind_rows(lapply(FACTORS, function(f) {
  kt <- kruskal.test(df[[r]] ~ df[[f]])
  data.frame(response = r, factor = f, H = unname(kt$statistic),
             df = unname(kt$parameter), p = kt$p.value,
             eps2 = (unname(kt$statistic) - nlevels(df[[f]]) + 1) / (nrow(df) - nlevels(df[[f]])))
}))))

# The screening is only worth reporting beside the model it screens for, so the
# ART main-effect size and the ordering each method gives are carried along.
art_main <- eff %>%
  filter(effect %in% FACTORS) %>%
  select(response, factor = effect, art_eta2p = eta_p2, art_p = p)
kw <- kw %>%
  left_join(art_main, by = c("response", "factor")) %>%
  group_by(response) %>%
  mutate(kw_rank = rank(-eps2), art_rank = rank(-art_eta2p)) %>%
  ungroup()
knitr::kable(kw, digits = 4)
```

```{r dunn}
dunn_rows <- list()
for (r in RESPONSES) for (f in FACTORS) {
  # Dunn's test is a post-hoc for more than two groups; with two levels the
  # Kruskal-Wallis test above already is the comparison, and FSA errors out.
  if (nlevels(df[[f]]) < 3) {
    cat(sprintf("skipping Dunn for %s: only %d levels, Kruskal-Wallis is the comparison\n",
                f, nlevels(df[[f]])))
    next
  }
  dt <- FSA::dunnTest(df[[r]] ~ df[[f]], method = "holm")$res
  dt$response <- r; dt$factor <- f
  dunn_rows[[paste(r, f)]] <- dt
}
dunn <- bind_rows(dunn_rows)
knitr::kable(head(dunn, 20), digits = 4)
```

# Selecting the operating configuration

```{r config}
cfg <- df %>% group_by(across(all_of(FACTORS))) %>%
  summarise(F1 = mean(F1), MAE = mean(MAE), F1_sd = sd(F1), MAE_sd = sd(MAE),
            .groups = "drop")

is_dominated <- function(i, d) any(d$F1 >= d$F1[i] & d$MAE <= d$MAE[i] &
                                   (d$F1 > d$F1[i] | d$MAE < d$MAE[i]))
cfg$pareto <- !sapply(seq_len(nrow(cfg)), is_dominated, d = cfg)
cfg$selected <- with(cfg, roi_size == SELECTED$roi_size & max_crops == SELECTED$max_crops &
                       mode == SELECTED$mode & abs(as.numeric(as.character(thresh)) - SELECTED$thresh) < 1e-9 &
                       pool_ks == SELECTED$pool_ks)
knitr::kable(head(arrange(cfg, desc(F1)), 8), digits = 4, caption = "Top 8 by F1")
knitr::kable(head(arrange(cfg, MAE), 8), digits = 4, caption = "Top 8 by MAE")
```

```{r fig-pareto, fig.width=4.6, fig.height=3.4}
# point, so a reader can tell which configuration each extreme is without
# going to the table.  Labelling every point is illegible at this width.
pareto_fig <- function(dat, lab_rows, name, nudge, w = 4.6, h = 3.4) {
  front <- dat %>% filter(pareto) %>% arrange(MAE)
  p <- ggplot(dat, aes(F1, MAE)) +
    geom_point(colour = WARM[2], alpha = 0.40, size = 0.8) +
    geom_line(data = front, colour = MUTED, linewidth = 1.3 / .pt) +
    geom_point(data = front, colour = INK, size = 1.3) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lab_rows, aes(label = lab),
                             size = 6.2 / .pt, colour = INK2, family = FONT,
                             seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0,
                             segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = WARM[2],
                             box.padding = 0.4, point.padding = 0.2,
                             nudge_y = nudge, direction = "both") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.06)) +
    labs(x = "F1-score", y = "MAE") + theme_thesis() +
    theme(axis.text  = element_text(colour = INK2, size = 7, family = FONT),
          axis.title = element_text(colour = INK, size = 8, family = FONT))
  if ("selected" %in% names(dat))
    p <- p + geom_point(data = filter(dat, selected), shape = 21, size = 2.6,
                        stroke = 0.6, colour = ACCENT, fill = NA)
  print(p)
  path <- file.path(FIGDIR, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(path, p, width = w, height = h, device = "pdf", family = FONT)
}

lab_of <- function(d) sprintf("roi %s, %s crops, ks %s", d$roi_size, d$max_crops, d$pool_ks)

# the factorial front
cfg <- df %>% group_by(across(all_of(FACTORS))) %>%
  summarise(F1 = mean(F1), MAE = mean(MAE), .groups = "drop")
cfg$pareto <- !sapply(seq_len(nrow(cfg)), function(i)
  any(cfg$F1 >= cfg$F1[i] & cfg$MAE <= cfg$MAE[i] &
      (cfg$F1 > cfg$F1[i] | cfg$MAE < cfg$MAE[i])))
cfg$selected <- cfg$roi_size == 9 & cfg$max_crops == 90 & cfg$mode == "average" &
  abs(as.numeric(as.character(cfg$thresh)) - 0.58) < 1e-9 & cfg$pool_ks == 9
fr <- filter(cfg, pareto)
labs <- fr[fr$F1 == max(fr$F1) | fr$MAE == min(fr$MAE) | fr$selected, ]
labs$lab <- ifelse(labs$selected, paste0(lab_of(labs), "\n(selected)"), lab_of(labs))
pareto_fig(cfg, labs, "grid_pareto_front", nudge = 5)

# the pooled Optuna trials
oks <- bind_rows(lapply(c("optuna1_results.csv", "optuna2_results.csv"), read.csv)) %>%
  transmute(roi_size, max_crops, pool_ks, F1 = f1_center, MAE = mae) %>%
  filter(F1 > 0, !is.na(MAE))
oks$pareto <- !sapply(seq_len(nrow(oks)), function(i)
  any(oks$F1 >= oks$F1[i] & oks$MAE <= oks$MAE[i] &
      (oks$F1 > oks$F1[i] | oks$MAE < oks$MAE[i])))
fo <- filter(oks, pareto)
labo <- fo[fo$F1 == max(fo$F1) | fo$MAE == min(fo$MAE), ]
labo$lab <- lab_of(labo)
pareto_fig(oks, labo, "optuna_scatter_pareto", nudge = 12)
```

# Marginal means

```{r boot-ci}
set.seed(42); B_BOOT <- 5000
boot_ci <- function(x, B = B_BOOT) {
  m <- replicate(B, mean(sample(x, length(x), replace = TRUE)))
  c(mean = mean(x), lo = unname(quantile(m, .025)), hi = unname(quantile(m, .975)))
}
ci <- bind_rows(lapply(RESPONSES, function(r) bind_rows(lapply(FACTORS, function(fc)
  df %>% group_by(level = .data[[fc]]) %>%
    summarise(as.data.frame(t(boot_ci(.data[[r]]))), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(response = r, factor = fc, .before = 1)))))
ci$level  <- lev_key(ci$factor, ci$level)
ci$factor <- base::factor(ci$factor, levels = FACTORS)
knitr::kable(head(ci, 12), digits = 4)
```

# Interaction figures

```{r fig-interactions, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=5.0}
eta <- setNames(eff$eta_p2, paste(eff$response, eff$effect))

ramp <- function(fc) WARM[round(seq(1, length(WARM), length.out = nlevels(df[[fc]])))]

PAIRS <- combn(FACTORS, 2, simplify = FALSE)
PAIRS <- PAIRS[order(-sapply(PAIRS, function(p)
  eta[[paste("MAE", paste(p, collapse = ":"))]]))]

panel <- function(pr, resp) {
  a <- pr[1]; b <- pr[2]
  # The factor with more levels goes on the horizontal axis, so that a curve
  # is traced by as many points as possible and as few lines as possible have
  # to be told apart by shade.  This puts mode, with two levels, always in
  # colour, and holds every panel to four lines or fewer.  Ties keep the order
  # of the design.
  if (nlevels(df[[b]]) > nlevels(df[[a]])) { a <- pr[2]; b <- pr[1] }
  cm <- df %>% group_by(.x = .data[[a]], .tr = .data[[b]]) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(.data[[resp]]), .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(cm, aes(.x, value, colour = .tr, group = .tr)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.3 / .pt) + geom_point(size = 1.1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = ramp(b), name = b) +
    scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 4) +
    # The factor name starts where the first key does, not centred over them.
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, title.position = "top",
                                 title.hjust = 0, label.position = "right",
                                 override.aes = list(linewidth = 0.8 / .pt, size = 0.5))) +
    labs(x = a, y = NULL)
}

for (r in RESPONSES) {
  g <- wrap_plots(lapply(PAIRS, panel, resp = r), nrow = 2) +
    plot_annotation(theme = theme(plot.background =
                                    element_rect(fill = SURFACE, colour = NA)))
  path <- file.path("figures", paste0("grid_interactions_", r, ".pdf"))
  print(g)
  ggsave(path, g, width = 8.2, height = 5.0, device = "pdf", family = FONT)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("figure was not written: ", path)
  cat("wrote", path, sprintf("(%.0f kB)\n", file.size(path) / 1024))
}

```

```{r fig-3way, fig.width=5.9, fig.height=1.6}
# --- the three-way terms of Section 6.4.5 ---------------------------------
# Each panel holds one level of the conditioning factor and traces the pair
# inside it, so the three-way term is the change of the pair from panel to
# panel.  The four of them share this reading.
three_way <- function(x, colr, facet, resp, h = 2.4, base = 8.5) {
  cm <- df %>% group_by(.f = .data[[facet]], .x = .data[[x]], .tr = .data[[colr]]) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(.data[[resp]]), .groups = "drop")
  ggplot(cm, aes(.x, value, colour = .tr, group = .tr)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.0 / .pt) + geom_point(size = 1.0) +
    facet_wrap(~.f, nrow = 1, labeller = labeller(.f = function(v) paste0(facet, ": ", v))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = ramp(colr), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = x, y = NULL) +
    theme_thesis(base) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank(),
          legend.text = element_text(colour = INK2, size = 7, family = FONT),
          axis.text = element_text(colour = INK2, size = 6.5, family = FONT),
          axis.title.x = element_text(colour = INK, size = 7.5, family = FONT),
          strip.text = element_text(colour = INK, size = 7.5, family = FONT))
}

# Ordered as Section 6.4.5 discusses them, by magnitude on the MAE.
for (sp in list(
  list(f = "grid_interaction_3way_crops_mode_thresh", x = "max_crops", c = "mode",  fa = "thresh"),
  list(f = "grid_interaction_3way_crops_mode_ks", x = "max_crops", c = "mode",      fa = "pool_ks"),
  list(f = "grid_interaction_3way_mode_thresh_ks", x = "thresh",   c = "mode",      fa = "pool_ks"),
  list(f = "grid_interaction_3way_crops_thresh_ks", x = "thresh",  c = "max_crops", fa = "pool_ks"))) {
  p <- three_way(sp$x, sp$c, sp$fa, "MAE")
  path <- file.path("figures", paste0(sp$f, ".pdf"))
  print(p)
  ggsave(path, p, width = 5.9, height = 1.60, device = "pdf", family = FONT)
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("figure was not written: ", path)
  cat("wrote", path, sprintf("(%.0f kB)\n", file.size(path) / 1024))
}
```
